title: Carrots, canned, reduced sodium, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Canned carrots with reduced sodium are made from selected carrot roots that are blanched, then cooked in butter or margarine and sealed in airtight jars. The lower salt level makes the product suitable for low‑sodium diets, while the added fat enhances flavor and improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Carrots have been cultivated for over 5,000 years and are one of the oldest cultivated vegetables.
Canning preserves the nutritional value of carrots for 2–3 years when stored properly.
Reduced sodium is achieved by replacing part of the salt with natural herbs and spices.
Cooking in butter or margarine increases the bioavailability of beta‑carotene, a precursor of vitamin A.
Carrots are rich in antioxidants such as lutein and zeaxanthin, which support eye health.

items.title: High in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is converted in the body to vitamin A, essential for vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure, and the reduced sodium content lessens strain on the heart.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin protect cells from oxidative stress, promoting healthy eyes.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 35 kcal, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Carrot allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to carrots, ranging from itching to swelling.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Because the product is cooked in butter or margarine, individuals monitoring saturated fat intake should account for this.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Although reduced, the product still contains salt; those with severe hypertension should consider it in their daily limit.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned carrots can be eaten cold in salads, added to soups, stews, and side dishes, used as a sandwich filling, or incorporated into baby foods. They can also be gently warmed in a skillet with a little extra butter.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened jar in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated in its original container and consume within 5–7 days. Discard if the jar bulges, leaks, or develops an off odor.
